scope: Diagnosis of the J1-R4 failure, the RC7 package and the J1-R5 local preparation (inputs, command plan, acceptance and runner). Local only; nothing ran on Linux, systemd or PostgreSQL and no host contact occurred.
ownerDecision: 2026-10-11 18:30 UTC: analyse the J1-R4 failure, build RC7 with tests and audit, then ask for a new GO. The owner later said work could continue while they were away; no GO was given.

diagnosis.ioReadback: The RC6 code formats the IO bandwidth limits for systemd as 20M and 40M (the host command line was not captured). systemd parses IO*BandwidthMax suffixes in base 1000, and the receipt recorded a kernel read-back of 20,000,000 and 40,000,000 bytes per second against a plan of 20,971,520 and 41,943,040, so the driver's strict read-back stopped the job before PostgreSQL started.
diagnosis.stopProofParse: The driver's stop proof parser accepted only lowercase letters and underscores in cgroup keys; kernel 6.8 cpu.stat carries core_sched.force_idle_usec when CONFIG_SCHED_CORE is set (expected on Ubuntu generic kernels, not verified on the host). This cause is about 90% likely and was not confirmed on the host.
diagnosis.method: Two Opus debuggers, read-only on the J1-R4 bundle and the code; a Fable second opinion agreed.

correction.recorded: The planned values are 20,000,000 and 40,000,000 bytes per second; the exact read-back value was not recorded.
correction.correct: The plan was 20,971,520 and 41,943,040 bytes per second. The recorded read-back was 20,000,000 and 40,000,000 bytes per second on the whole disk device. The cause is the base-1000 suffix parsing above.

changes: IO bandwidth limits are passed as plain integer bytes; memory and file-size limits keep the base-1024 form
cgroup parsers accept real kernel keys and spacing; repeated io.max fields or device lines refuse; ENODEV counts as absent only for cgroup files
a HOST_PARSE in a cleanup step is logged with a short allowlisted label
cgroup and SQL monitor read timeouts count toward the existing four-failure limit; the du watchdog still stops at once
before any write or launch the controller checks that the unit IO properties are digits equal to the plan bytes (IO_ARGV_MISMATCH)
preflight checks 16 PostgreSQL runtime files: 15 that initdb and server start need, plus english.stop as a fail-closed extra (PG_SHARE_MISSING)
the outer proof adds an ioLimits check against the driver's recorded read-back when that read-back succeeded
rc7.unchanged: receipt.mjs, sanitize.mjs and the other 9 adapters (RC6 bytes), harness v8.2, measurement tool v3, product revision eb532ffd, the RC6 timer rule, every job limit

reviews: Three Opus audits (RC7 rounds 1 and 2, J1-R5 preparation): the one medium finding was closed in round 2, and the low items are disclosed in the GO packet. Fable 5.1 gave four second opinions (diagnosis, RC7 rounds 1 and 2, J1-R5 preparation) and one consistency check of this record; its stopword point was refuted against PostgreSQL source. disclosures: initdb, PostgreSQL start, the suite socket confinement, the monitor samples and the final cgroup statistics have never run on Linux in this job path
whether the 16 PostgreSQL runtime files exist in the bound runtime tree is unknown; a missing one refuses at preflight after the new paths are written and consumes the attempt
a stop before PostgreSQL starts ends as <code>+STOP_PROOF_FAILED from the frozen v8.2 runner
the IO outer check uses the driver's recorded read-back, not an independent kernel read
jobPidsMax 26 and the shared 512 MiB unit memory are tight
the boot pin currency after any reboot is unknown
the J1-R4 job base, inputs and RC6 package root stay on the host
whether the host has the system time zone data the Debian PostgreSQL build expects is unknown
